Picks and Parlays NFL handicapper Steve Seagrave breaks down his top NFL player prop picks for Week 4 across several of the biggest games on the schedule. This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. NFL player props are bets on a specific statistical outcome for a specific NFL player. We cover passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards, and anytime touchdowns in our tool, but there are countless other betting opportunities every week. Every prop bet has two parts: The number (Over or Under 81.5 rushing yards, for example) The price, which determines how much a winning bet returns and reflects the implied probability If two players are lined at 45.5 receiving yards, that does not necessarily mean they have the same implied odds. Player A — Over 45.5 receiving yards (-115) — 53.5% implied over probability — Winning $100 bet has $187 return Player B — Over 45.5 receiving yards (+105) — 48.8% implied over probability — Winning $100 bet has $205 return When Do NFL Player Props Come Out Each Week? After favorites wrecked Week 9, the underdogs got out to an early win. I have three early picks for primetime games in Germany, Cincinnati, and Baltimore. Best of luck and enjoy the weekend! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Lions (-2.5) vs Patriots: O/U 51.5 The Lions and Patriots will meet in Munich, Germany, with a potential shootout on our hands. Last week, Green Bay torched New England’s secondary for almost 400 passing yards, and the Patriots face Detroit, which hasn’t had to throw the last two games. Jared Goff has thrown 25 pass attempts in each of his past two games against the Dolphins and Vikings and gone under 200 yards. Goff hasn’t gone under 200 passing yards in back-to-back games since 2024. Before the previous two games, Goff threw at least 30 passes in six straight and 38 or more in three. This is a spot where I think he clears 30 and could approach 40 pass attempts. The Patriots run the second-most man coverage (28.5%), and that opens the door for this Lions offense. Detroit scored 31 on the Jets, and Goff went 25-of-32 for 269 yards and two touchdowns; and that’s important because that’s the only game that Goff has faced against a team ranked top 10 in man coverage rate. The Patriots are obviously a step up from the Jets defensively, and after the New England secondary was trashed by Jordan Love , Christian Watson , and Matthew Golden last week, this prop just seems that much better. I like Goff Over 34.5 pass attempts up to 35.5. The only quarterback who’s gone for 35-plus against New England is Aaron Rodgers (39) , but that’s about to change. I also added Drake Maye to go Over 33.5 pass attempts and Over 1.5 passing touchdowns. Maye is basically the offense at this point and he has a good matchup with Detroit. The fact that A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson are back helps Maye out, but they aren’t 100-percent, and neither is the Pats offensive line (down 2 starters). Maye has thrown two-plus touchdowns in six-straight games and I think that could continue against a Lions defense that allows a lot of explosives through the air. This could be a shoot out and New England is getting desperate. Picks: Jared Goff Over 34.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Drake Maye Over 33.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Maye over 1.5 Pass TDs (1 unit) Chiefs (-3) at Falcons: O/U 47.5 No Kenneth Walker opens the door for Patrick Mahomes to have a day. The Falcons’ opponents have the ninth-highest pass rate over exception this season, and it’s third if you remove the Buccaneers game where Baker Mayfield threw three times in a monsoon. Atlanta is allowing 228.0 passing yards per game, but remove that Mayfield performance and the number rises to 271.3, which would rank last in the NFL. Here is the list of quarterbacks and how they’ve performed this season against Atlanta. Joe Burrow: 271 Baker Mayfield: 0 Brock Purdy: 288 Caleb Williams: 305 Tyler Huntley: 201 Tyler Shough: 286 Jordan Love: 312 Bryce Young: 287 Aaron Rodgers: 221 Six out of nine quarterbacks went over 240 passing yards, including three of the last four, and six of the past eight. Mahomes has thrown for at least 240 passing yards in five of eight games and two straight. Emmett Johnson has a surprising rushing prop of 71.5 and a rush + rec prop of 102.5, so he may get a heavy dosage, but in a dome setting, I think Kansas City reverts to trusting Mahomes more. I think he adds another to his resume in Atlanta. I’d go up to 244.5. This prop was 236.5 yesterday. Pick: Patrick Mahomes 240+ Passing Yards (1 unit) Jaguars (-10.5) at Titans: O/U 46.5 I lost on Tony Pollard ‘s under rushing yards last week against the Bengals, but will run it back on his Under. Pollard has 129 and 117 rushing yards in back-to-back games on 25 and 21 carries, plus five touchdowns. Both game scripts worked out that Tennessee was in the game until the final whistle, so running the ball was never out of the question. However, that could change here. Not only could the bye week throw off the ground game’s rhythm, but this matchup is the toughest of the season on paper. In the last three games, Derrick Henry was held to 57 rushing yards last week, and Jonathan Taylor to 23 yards two weeks ago, plus Woody Marks had 56 yards. Jacksonville ranks fifth in the NFL with 89.3 rushing yards allowed per game, but that also dropped after Justice Hill had a garbage-time 65-yard run last week. Pollard has hit the over in three straight games and is 5-3 to the over on the season. I’m buying into regression hitting this week. I’m taking the under 58.5 rushing yards down to 53.5. I expect a negative game script and Pollard’s role in the pass game to increase here, and his carries regress back to the norm. Last season, Pollard ran for 60 and 48 yards against the Jaguars on 10 and 14 carries. Jacksonville won by 22 and 34 points. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 58.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Vikings at Packers (-3): O/U 42.5 Did you know that Jordan Love is the only quarterback to throw for two touchdowns against the Vikings this season? That was in Week 1, so seven-straight quarterbacks have thrown for one or fewer touchdowns against Minnesota. Well, fast forward to Week 10, and Green Bay still doesn’t have a running game, so Love has carried the offense. If the Packers are to score more than two touchdowns in this game, it’s hard for me to see it not coming from the arm of Love. He is 8-1 to the over 1.5 passing touchdowns this season. I’ll take him to go Over 1.5 passing touchdowns against Minnesota again and ride his heater of three-straight overs. Outside boundary receivers have had a hard time against Minnesota this season, but one wideout that burned the Vikings defense was Matthew Golden . He’s burned me too. I faded Golden the past two weeks, and he snuck over with 79 yards, then had a monster 164 yards against New England. This becomes a fade spot of a career-high and after catching all 10 targets. I am going under 71.5 yards on Golden, down to 66.5. I’ll root for a red zone touchdown from him, though. The Steelers and Bengals are both on four-game winning streaks, and the winner will be in first place in the AFC North. The spread and total for this first game were Bengals -3.5 and 42.5, so we have a full seven-point correction on the total for the second game after Pittsburgh won 30-27 in Week 3. Pittsburgh has been money in years past with Mike Tomlin coming off a bye week (17-5 ML), but this Mike McCarthy’s team now, plus the Bengals, are incredible when at a rest disadvantage. Since 2019 with Zac Taylor , the Bengals are 18-5-1 ATS with a rest disadvantage. Rather than picking a side, I am going under 24.5 points in the first half. An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Most player props are offered as over/under bets. For example, a sportsbook might set a quarterback's passing yards at 245.5. A team that falls behind by three scores is likely to throw more and run less, which can boost passing and receiving opportunities while cutting into rushing volume. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images My early Week 11 NFL player props start with two running backs coming off very different Sundays James Cook broke a 74-yard run for Buffalo, while Christian McCaffrey did most of his damage as a receiver See my three Week 11 NFL prop picks and projected lines below James Cook ran for 157 yards against the Jets. Christian McCaffrey had 161 yards receiving against Dallas. Both performances will draw attention to their Week 11 NFL player props, but I’d approach their rushing totals very differently. Last week, two of my three early targets cleared their projected lines. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 171 receiving yards and Ja’Marr Chase caught 11 passes. McCaffrey fell three rushing yards short, even as he scored three touchdowns. Cook gets Miami in Buffalo, McCaffrey faces Minnesota in Mexico City and Chase visits Washington on Monday night. Even his best game, a 75-yard afternoon against Arizona, would have beaten my projected line by just half a yard. McCaffrey has had seven, 18 and 13 carries in his last three games. Las Vegas was the one opponent in that stretch against whom he got a steady afternoon of handoffs. He finished with 68 yards. Dallas gave up 161 receiving yards to McCaffrey on just four catches. I want his rushing under if the line opens in the mid-70s: he can hurt Minnesota on a screen or a wheel route without adding a yard to his rushing total. Minnesota has allowed 4.2 yards per carry on 241 attempts. The workload I’d worry about is 18 or 19 carries. At 13, the number he got in Dallas, he’d need a gain of nearly six yards per attempt to beat me. My cutoff matters here. If the opening line lands near the 62 yards he put up in Dallas, I’d pass. In the mid-70s, I’m happy to let his receiving yards grab the headlines. Early Bet: Christian McCaffrey under 74.5 rushing yards (estimated target) NFL Player Prop Pick #2: James Cook Rushing Yards When I compare rushing yards odds , James Cook is the back I want at 89.5. He’s rushed for at least 90 yards in six of nine games, including five of the six in which Buffalo gave him 20 or more carries. Cook has 344 rushing yards on 70 attempts over his last three games. Two of those afternoons show why I’d play the over against Miami, even if the Dolphins keep him from breaking another long touchdown. 74-YARD TD FOR JAMES COOK BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DFRLVP17FL — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Cook’s 74-yard touchdown against the Jets accounted for nearly half of his 157 yards. His other 17 carries went for 83, seven short of what I’m looking for against the Dolphins. The Minnesota game is why I don’t need a repeat of that highlight. Cook’s longest run against the Vikings went for 11 yards. He still finished with 107 because Buffalo went back to him 31 times. Miami has allowed 1,066 rushing yards on 270 attempts, 4.0 per carry, without giving up a run longer than 27 yards in that sample. Teams have kept running on them, which suits how Cook piles up yardage. If Buffalo falls behind and has to throw, the cushion disappears. Cook had just 57 yards on 13 carries in Houston and 75 on 12 against New England. I’m backing him to get closer to his usual workload at home. Early Bet: James Cook over 89.5 rushing yards (estimated target) NFL Player Prop Pick #3: Ja’Marr Chase Receptions For Ja’Marr Chase’s receptions prop against Washington, I’m looking at how quickly Cincinnati’s passing game has shifted. Chase caught 32 passes in his last three games. It took all six of his previous games combined to catch that many. He went for 11 catches against Tennessee, 10 against Atlanta and 11 against Pittsburgh. He’s reached eight in four of nine games overall, so this pick depends on Cincinnati continuing to feed him the way it has over the last three games. The Pittsburgh highlight is the 231 receiving yards. For NFL total receptions props , I give the Atlanta game just as much weight. Chase cleared this target by two catches there without needing anything close to 231 yards. Washington has allowed 217 receptions for 2,341 receiving yards to all positions this season. That total includes backs and tight ends, so it tells us what opponents have done through the air, not which receiver will get the ball. Eight catches is where I’d draw the line for Chase. I’d play the over at 7.5 on Monday night. At 8.5, the price of admission becomes a ninth catch, something Chase managed just once in those first six games. That’s where I’d stop.
